extracted.intended_audience: F-1 students, designated school officials (DSOs), SEVP-certified schools, immigration practitioners, and USCIS adjudicators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards governing admission, maintenance of status, employment, transfers, practical training, and related SEVIS/DSO actions for F-1 nonimmigrant students under 8 CFR 214.2(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of inadmissibility for E-2 CNMI Investor status
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien otherwise admissible to the United States who has provided all appropriate documents as described may be granted a waiver of inadmissibility under section 212(d)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act for the purpose of granting E-2 CNMI Investor nonimmigrant status; such waiver may be granted without additional form or fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes waiver for certain grounds described in 212(a)(6)(A)(i) and 212(a)(7)(B)(i)(II) to the extent they arise solely because of presence in the CNMI on Nov 28, 2009. For spouse/child applicants present in the CNMI, required documents include a valid unexpired passport and evidence of lawful presence in the CNMI under 48 U.S.C. 1806(e) (may include evidence of parole or advance parole).

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of student — Eligibility for admission
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonimmigrant student may be admitted in F-1 status if they present a Form I-20 or successor form issued in the student's name by an SEVP-certified school, have documentary evidence of financial support as indicated on the I-20, (for initial admission) intend to attend the school specified on the visa or I-20, and, for public secondary school students, have reimbursed the local educational agency the full unsubsidized per capita cost of education for their attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Form I-20 must be issued by a school certified by SEVP for attendance by F-1 foreign students. Evidence of financial support must match amounts on the Form I-20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-20 requirements at port-of-entry
rubrics_metrics.description: When an F-1 student applies for admission with a complete Form I-20 or successor form, the inspecting officer will transcribe the student's admission number from Form I-94 onto the Form I-20 (for initial admission only), endorse the Form I-20, and return it to the student.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SEVIS by schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools must issue a Form I-20 or successor form in SEVIS to any current student requiring a reportable action (e.g., extension of stay, practical training, requests for employment authorization), or to any alien who must obtain a new nonimmigrant student visa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reportable actions must be reflected in SEVIS; schools must maintain SEVIS records for students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student maintenance of Form I-20
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 student is expected to retain the initial Form I-20 and any subsequent I-20; if lost, the DSO should issue a replacement copy bearing the same information, including any endorsements for employment and notations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement I-20 should bear the same admission number and endorsements as the lost copy; DSOs are responsible for issuing replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of spouse and minor children of F-1 student
rubrics_metrics.description: Spouse and minor children accompanying or following-to-join an F-1 student are eligible for F-2 status and must individually present a Form I-20 or successor form in their name issued by an SEVP-certified school. A new I-20 is required for a dependent when there has been any substantive change in the F-1 student's current information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For following-to-join, dependents must demonstrate the F-1 student has been admitted and is or will be enrolled within 30 days or engaged in approved practical training following completion of studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary absence — readmission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 student returning from a temporary absence of five months or less may be readmitted for attendance if they present either a current I-20 properly endorsed by the DSO for reentry (if no substantive change) or an updated I-20 if there has been a substantive change (e.g., change of major, transfer, advance to higher level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If substantive change occurred, the student must present the updated I-20 to reenter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of status — definition and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of status is the time during which an F-1 student is pursuing a full course of study at an SEVP-certified institution or engaging in authorized practical training after studies; F-1 students admitted to attend a public high school are restricted to an aggregate of 12 months of study at any public high school(s). Students may be admitted up to 30 days before the report date/program start date and are considered to be maintaining status if making normal progress toward completing the course of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal progress and program-specific limits apply; 30-day early admission limit is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in educational levels maintains status
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 student who continues from one educational level to another is considered maintaining status provided the transition is accomplished according to transfer procedures in paragraph (f)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual vacation status rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 student at an academic institution is in status during annual (or summer) vacation if eligible and intending to register for the next term. Students on quarter/trimester calendars who take one vacation during a quarter/trimester are in status during that vacation if they completed the equivalent of an academic year prior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation for departure periods
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 student who has completed a course of study and any authorized practical training gets an additional 60-day period to prepare for departure or transfer; an F-1 student authorized by the DSO to withdraw is allowed 15 days to depart. Students failing to maintain a full course of study without DSO approval are not eligible for these additional periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergent circumstances exception for employment and enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Secretary suspends applicability of on-/off-campus employment requirements by Federal Register notice, affected students who need to reduce their full course of study due to accepting authorized employment will be considered in status during the authorized employment, subject to conditions in the notice, provided they remain registered for the semester/quarter hours specified (minimums: 6 semester/quarter hours undergraduate; 3 for graduate) and continue to make progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Register notice specifies required hours and any other conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic extension of F-1 duration of status and employment for H-1B cap beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 student's duration of status and any employment authorization will be automatically extended until April 1 of the fiscal year for which an H-1B status is requested or until the approved petition's validity start date, whichever is earlier, where the H-1B petition: (1) has been timely filed; (2) requests an H-1B employment start date in the fiscal year requested; and (3) is nonfrivolous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The automatic extension terminates upon rejection, denial, revocation, or withdrawal of the H-1B petition or denial/withdrawal of the change-of-status request. Student must not have violated nonimmigrant status per 8 CFR part 248. Extension also applies to F-2 dependents' duration of status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full course of study — general definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'full course of study' must lead to a specific educational/professional objective; study at institutions not SEVP-certified does not satisfy requirement. Definitions include postgraduate/postdoctoral study, undergraduate minimums, language program rules, clock-hour standards for non-vocational programs, and elementary/middle/high school attendance minimums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key subrules: (A) postgraduate/postdoctoral study or undergraduate/postgraduate at conservatory/seminary certified by DSO; (B) undergraduate = at least 12 semester/quarter hours or equivalent where 12 hours equals full-time for tuition/administrative purposes; (C) postsecondary language/liberal arts programs must confer recognized associate/other degrees or have credits accepted unconditionally by at least 3 other institutions and be certified as at least 12 clock hours/week if classroom-dominant; (D) other language/liberal arts programs require 18 clock hours/week classroom-dominant or 22 clock hours/week if laboratory-dominant; (E) certified private elementary/middle or academic high schools must meet minimum hours prescribed by the school for normal progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online/distance education limits toward full course of study
rubrics_metrics.description: For F-1 students enrolled in classes for credit or classroom hours, no more than the equivalent of one class or three credits per session/term/semester/trimester/quarter may be counted toward the full course of study if the class is online/distance education that does not require physical attendance; language study programs may not count any online/distance education toward full course of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines online/distance education broadly (television, audio, computer transmission, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: On-campus employment considered part of academic program
rubrics_metrics.description: On-campus employment pursuant to scholarship, fellowship, or assistantship terms is deemed part of the academic program for students otherwise taking a full course of study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution of higher learning definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A college or university is an institution awarding recognized associate, bachelor's, master's, doctorate, or professional degrees; schools devoted primarily to vocational, business, or language instruction are not included as institutions of higher learning under this paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vocational/business schools classifiable as M-1 schools are governed by 8 CFR 214.2(m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced course load — minimum and out-of-status rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A DSO may allow an F-1 student to engage in less than a full course of study; except as noted, a reduced course load must consist of at least six semester/quarter hours or half the clock hours required for a full course of study. A student who drops below full course without prior DSO approval is out of status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-campus employment as scholarship/fellowship/assistantship counts toward the academic program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced course load authorization for academic difficulties
rubrics_metrics.description: DSO may authorize reduced course load for initial difficulty with English, unfamiliarity with U.S. teaching methods, or improper course placement. Student must resume full course at next available term (excluding summer). A student is not eligible for a second authorization for academic difficulties at the same program level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced course load authorization for medical conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: DSO may authorize reduced (or no) course load due to temporary illness or medical condition for period not to exceed aggregate 12 months at a program level. Student must provide current medical documentation from a licensed medical doctor, DO, licensed psychologist, or licensed clinical psychologist; DSO must reauthorize each new term. Aggregate limit of 12 months applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student previously authorized for 12 months aggregate cannot be authorized again for the same program level; multiple occasions permitted if aggregate ≤12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced course load for completion of course of study (final term)
rubrics_metrics.description: DSO may authorize reduced course load in the student's final term if fewer courses are needed to complete the program. If no additional courses are required and student continues enrolled for administrative purposes, they are considered to have completed the course and must take action to maintain status (e.g., change of status or departure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements for authorized reduced course load
rubrics_metrics.description: To authorize reduced course load, DSO must update SEVIS prior to the student reducing their course load, including date, reason, and start date of next term. DSO must notify SEVIS within 21 days of the student's commencement of a full course of study. If program end date extension is required, DSO must update SEVIS with a new I-20 reflecting the new program end date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent enrollment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 student may be enrolled in two different SEVP-certified schools concurrently as long as combined enrollment equals a full course of study. The school granting the degree/certification should issue the I-20 and conduct certifications and updates; that school's DSO is responsible for SEVIS reporting. Where programs have different full-course requirements, the DSO may determine what constitutes a full course of study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 student admitted for duration of status need not apply for extension of stay while maintaining status and making normal progress. A student who cannot complete by the program end date must apply before that date for a program extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report date and program completion date guidance for DSOs
rubrics_metrics.description: DSO may choose a reasonable report date to accommodate required pre-class activities (research, orientation), but may not indicate a report date more than 30 days prior for employment purposes. Program completion date should be a reasonable estimate based on time an average student would need to complete a similar program in the same discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program extension for students in lawful status
rubrics_metrics.description: DSO may grant program extension if student has continuously maintained status and delays are caused by compelling academic or medical reasons (e.g., change of major, unexpected research problems, documented illness). Delays caused by academic probation or suspension are not acceptable. DSO may not grant extension if student applies after the program end date. Students ineligible for extension may apply for reinstatement under paragraph (f)(16).

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS update requirement for program extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A DSO may grant a program extension only by updating SEVIS and issuing a new I-20 or successor form reflecting the current program end date. A DSO may grant an extension any time prior to the program end date on the student's I-20.

rubrics_metrics.name: School transfer — general eligibility and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A student maintaining status may transfer to another SEVP-certified school by following notification procedures; an F-1 student is not permitted to remain in the U.S. when transferring unless they will begin classes at transfer school within five months of transferring out or within five months of the program completion date, whichever is earlier. For students on post-completion OPT, they must resume classes within five months of transferring out of the school that recommended OPT or when OPT ends. Students not pursuing a full course at the prior school are ineligible for transfer and must apply for reinstatement or depart and reenter as an initial entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer procedure and SEVIS release/controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Student must notify the transfer-out school of intent to transfer and identify transfer-in school. Transfer-out school must update SEVIS to show transfer-out, indicate transfer-in school, and input transfer release date (current semester/session completion date or earlier expected transfer date). Transfer-out retains control of SEVIS record until release date; student or transfer-out DSO may cancel transfer before release date. As of the release date, transfer-in school receives full access and responsibility. Transfer-in DSO must complete the SEVIS transfer and may issue an I-20; student must contact transfer-in DSO within 15 days of program start date. Transfer is completed when transfer-in notifies SEVIS of student's enrollment in accordance with §214.3(g)(2)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: On-campus employment — definition and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: On-campus employment must be performed on school premises (including on-location commercial firms providing student services) or at off-campus locations educationally affiliated with the school. Employment with on-site commercial firms that do not provide direct student services (e.g., construction company building a school building) is not on-campus employment. For off-campus educationally affiliated locations, employment must be integral to the educational program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-campus employment must not exceed 20 hours/week when school is in session unless Secretary suspends the limitation; students may work full-time when school is not in session. A student may not begin on-campus employment more than 30 days prior to start of classes upon initial entry. Employment must not displace U.S. residents. In a SEVIS transfer, student may only engage in on-campus employment at the school controlling the SEVIS record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-campus work authorization — general
rubrics_metrics.description: An F-1 student may be authorized to work off-campus part-time after one full academic year in F-1 status, provided the student is in good academic standing as determined by the DSO. Part-time off-campus employment is limited to no more than 20 hours/week while school is in session; full-time may be worked during holidays or school vacation. Employment authorization is automatically terminated when student fails to maintain status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary may suspend applicability of off-campus work requirements in emergent circumstances via Federal Register notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severe economic hardship — qualifying circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Severe economic hardship may justify off-campus employment authorization when other employment opportunities are not available or insufficient, caused by unforeseen circumstances beyond the student's control, including loss of financial aid or on-campus employment without fault, substantial currency/exchange rate fluctuations, inordinate increases in tuition/living costs, unexpected changes in financial condition of support source, medical bills, or other substantial unexpected expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are illustrative, not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for off-campus employment authorization due to severe economic hardship
rubrics_metrics.description: Student must request a recommendation from the DSO, who must complete certification in SEVIS. The DSO may recommend work authorization for one-year intervals by certifying that the student: (1) has been in F-1 status for one full academic year; (2) is in good standing and carrying a full course of study; (3) has demonstrated that employment will not interfere with carrying a full course; and (4) has demonstrated employment is necessary to avoid severe economic hardship and on-campus employment is unavailable or insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severe economic hardship application process to USCIS
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should submit Form I-765 (or successor) with the fee required by 8 CFR 106.2 and supporting materials such as affidavits detailing unforeseen circumstances and unavailability of on-campus employment, and the I-20 with the DSO's comments/certification. USCIS will adjudicate on the basis of the I-20, I-765, and additional materials and will issue an EAD if authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will notify student of decision and reasons for denial; no appeal lies from a denial. Employment authorization may be granted in one-year intervals up to program completion date; renewals require maintaining status and good academic standing; authorization terminates automatically when student fails to maintain status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internship with an international organization — authorization requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A bona fide F-1 student offered employment by a recognized international organization must apply for employment authorization with USCIS and present: a written certification from the organization that the employment is within the scope of the organization's sponsorship, Form I-20 with employment page completed by DSO certifying eligibility, and a completed Form I-765 with the required fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical training — eligibility and general limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical training may be authorized to an F-1 student who has been lawfully enrolled full-time in an approved SEVP-certified institution for one full academic year (includes qualifying study abroad if at least one U.S. full academic term was completed prior). Students may be authorized 12 months of practical training and become eligible for another 12 months when changing to a higher educational level. Students in English language training programs are ineligible. Practical training must be directly related to the student's major.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical training must be requested/authorized per the curricular or optional categories described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curricular practical training (CPT) — authorization and SEVIS recording
rubrics_metrics.description: DSO may authorize curricular practical training that is an integral part of an established curriculum (alternative work/study, internship, cooperative education, required practicum) by updating SEVIS to show CPT authorization, indicating whether training is full-time or part-time, employer and location, and employment start/end dates. DSO must sign, date, and return the I-20 to the student prior to employment commencement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student may begin CPT only after receiving I-20 with DSO endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional practical training (OPT) — application and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A student may apply to USCIS for authorization for temporary employment for OPT directly related to the major area of study; the student may not begin OPT until the date on the EAD (Form I-766). OPT may be authorized: during annual vacation/when school not in session if enrolled and eligible; while school is in session not exceeding 20 hours/week; or after completion of course of study (or after completion of all course requirements excluding thesis) with completion of all OPT within a 14-month period except as modified by the 24-month STEM extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued administrative enrollment after satisfying degree requirements does not preclude OPT eligibility. Student must observe EAD start date and hours limits while school is in session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of optional practical training
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization for OPT is automatically terminated when the student transfers to another school or begins study at another educational level.

rubrics_metrics.name: 24-month STEM OPT extension — eligibility and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified student in a STEM degree may apply for a 24-month extension of post-completion OPT while in a valid period of post-completion OPT; extension applies to the first qualifying degree for which course requirements were completed (including qualifying degrees in dual programs) provided previously obtained degrees were conferred. If a student completes another qualifying degree at a higher level, they may apply for a second 24-month extension while in a valid period of post-completion OPT. No student may be authorized for more than two lifetime STEM OPT extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degrees used for STEM OPT extension must have been conferred. Specific regulatory conditions referenced in paragraph (f)(11)(i)(C) apply.
